newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish refineries to lift petrol prices next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish refineries to lift petrol prices next week.

text.p: Poland's two main oil refineries, Petrochemia Plock and Rafineria Gdansk, said on Friday they would increase petrol prices by nearly two percent next week and cut the diesel fuel price by one percent.

"The Gdansk refinery will raise the prices of petrol by three groszes (0.03 zloty) and lower the price of diesel fuel by one grosz (0.01 zloty) in coming days, probably on Monday," the refinery's spokeswoman Ewa Sielicka told Reuters.
The bigger Plock refinery announced the same price changes in a statement issued to reporters.

If retailers' fee and excise tax stay at the same level, the increase in wholesale prices would translate into retail prices of 1.65 zloty per litre of 94-octane leaded petrol, 1.61 zloty per litre of 95-octane unleaded petrol and 1.77 zloty for 98-octane unleaded petrol.
The retail price of diesel from Plock should be 1.39 zloty per litre while the price from Gdansk should come to 1.42 zloty per litre.
Prices of domestically-produced fuels have increased by between five and eight percent since they were freed by the finance ministry last month.
